title: Evaluating varied cases
goals: Separate development evidence from final checks

prerequisite.prompt: If final cases guide a code change, are they still untouched evaluation cases?
prerequisite.answer: No; they have become part of development evidence.

vocabulary: Cases used to assess a specified version
A type of scenario where an expected result is missed
Passing cases divided by executed cases
The variety of requirements and conditions tested

blocks.text: A fictional chooser passes 5 of 6 development checks but fails its only tie case. An overall pass rate can hide that concentrated weakness. Evaluate ordinary, boundary, invalid, empty and tie cases separately, using requirements rather than duplicated versions of one easy example.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
checks = [{"category": "ordinary", "passed": True},
          {"category": "ordinary", "passed": True},
          {"category": "boundary", "passed": True},
          {"category": "invalid", "passed": True},
          {"category": "empty", "passed": True},
          {"category": "tie", "passed": False}]
passed = 0
for check in checks:
    if check["passed"]:
        passed = passed + 1
print(passed, len(checks))

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The script reports 5 and 6. About 83.3 percent of these checks pass, but that is not an accuracy estimate for all future use. The cases were deliberately chosen, their frequencies are artificial, and each category has few cases.

blocks.label: If ten copies of one passing ordinary case are added, what becomes the pass fraction? Does coverage improve?

blocks.text: Hiding the tie failure in an average conceals an unmet requirement. Preserve the failed input, expected result, actual result and version. If you repair using it, classify it as development/regression evidence and reserve new final cases.

For a rule-based chooser, evaluate conformance to its policy separately from whether users find suggestions useful. Neither a pass fraction nor an invented satisfaction score proves educational benefit.

blocks.label: You fix the tie bug using the final tie case. What should the next evaluation report say?

workbook.title: Read denominators
workbook.prompt: A report says 8 of 10 tests pass, including 0 of 2 invalid-input cases. What is the important weakness?
workbook.answer: Invalid-input handling fails both tested cases even though the overall pass fraction is 80 percent.

workbook.title: Plan coverage
workbook.prompt: Name five distinct categories for the chooser evaluation.
workbook.answer: Ordinary selection, duration boundaries, invalid records, empty/no-match input and ties/order reversal.

workbook.title: Repair reporting
workbook.prompt: A learner drops two failed cases and reports 8/8. What should be restored?
workbook.answer: Report all 10 executed cases with 8 passes and 2 failures, category details and the tested version.

workbook.title: Evaluate independently
workbook.prompt: Given ordinary 3/3, boundary 1/2, invalid 2/2 and tie 0/1, compute overall results and prioritize issues.
workbook.answer: 6/8 pass, 2 fail; boundary has one failure and ties fail the only case. Report both and avoid treating 75 percent as production accuracy.

workbook.title: Protect final evidence
workbook.prompt: You fix the tie bug using the final tie case. What should the next evaluation report say?
workbook.answer: The old case is now a regression/development case. Document the fix and use fresh reserved cases for a new independent final check.

teacher.background: Teach Week 34 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional chooser passes 5 of 6 development checks but fails its only tie case. An overall pass rate can hide that concentrated weakness. Evaluate ordinary, boundary, invalid, empty and tie cases separately, using requirements rather than duplicated versions of one easy example. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.
materials: Python 3 editor with a fresh local practice file
Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.
Read the worked example and diagram; ask learners to trace each step aloud.
Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
teacher.guidedAnswer: 15/16 pass, but no new condition was tested. The larger fraction is misleading as evidence of broader quality. Exit: The old case is now a regression/development case. Document the fix and use fresh reserved cases for a new independent final check.
misconceptions: A successful run proves the conclusion

For a rule-based chooser, evaluate conformance to its policy separately from whether users find suggestions useful. Neither a pass fraction nor an invented satisfaction score proves educational benefit.

Require the new W4 case, explicit predictions and an explanation. Fresh retry: ordinary 2/2, empty 0/1, boundary 2/2 gives 4/5 overall; the empty case still fails. Require the failure record and a fresh-case plan.

Hiding the tie failure in an average conceals an unmet requirement. Preserve the failed input, expected result, actual result and version. If you repair using it, classify it as development/regression evidence and reserve new final cases.
teacher.assessment: Independent W4 evidence: 6/8 pass, 2 fail; boundary has one failure and ties fail the only case. Report both and avoid treating 75 percent as production accuracy. Record whether the learner needed no help, a hint or explanation. Fresh retry: ordinary 2/2, empty 0/1, boundary 2/2 gives 4/5 overall; the empty case still fails. Require the failure record and a fresh-case plan.
teacher.support: Use a category-by-case grid. Extension: add a new case that tests a different failure mechanism rather than duplicating a passing case.
teacher.next: Next week: Improving without hiding failures. Reuse this week's explicit contracts and evidence.
